laws.rule: Chiba City bans smoking on the street in four enforcement districts: around JR Chiba Station east exit (enlarged in October 2026), JR Inage, JR Kaihin-Makuhari and JR Soga stations. Patrol officers collect a JPY 2,000 penalty on the spot (about A$18.05, RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = JPY 110.82). Dropping litter such as cigarette butts in outdoor public places anywhere in the city brings the same penalty. Heated tobacco is not covered by the smoking ban, but dropping its butts is.

laws.rule: Chiba Prefecture does not yet charge an accommodation tax. It published a draft system for public comment (26 June to 24 July 2026) and says it will make a Chiba Prefecture Accommodation Tax ordinance after weighing the comments. The comment results were posted on 9 October 2026 (35 people, 111 comments). The page gives no start date or rate.

For drone flying or filming on coasts and rivers the prefecture manages (not port or fishing-port areas), Chiba Prefecture asks you to consult the civil engineering office (doboku jimusho) for the municipality first. The page names no set permit and reminds operators that the Aviation Act still applies. Some coasts and rivers belong to national or city managers, and the office will point you to them.

Kashiwa City (Chiba) bans walking while smoking and littering on all city roads. Smoking on the street elsewhere is allowed only if you stop where you do not block others and use a portable ashtray. Around Kashiwa Station a 'strengthened' zone bans smoking in public places and portable ashtrays do not make it allowed. A fine of JPY 2,000 (about A$18.05, RBA rate of 30 October 2026) applies in that zone; the ordinance began on 1 April 2005 and the fine on 1 October 2005.
